description:
The resolver sweeps conflict history older than version_retention_ms (default 6s) via remove_old_conflicts (server.ex:237, conflicts.ex:121). But check_conflicts (conflicts.ex:53) has no floor check: it walks version entries > read_version and returns :ok if none overlap. If a transaction arrives with a read_version older than the pruned horizon, writes that occurred in the pruned range are invisible and the transaction COMMITS instead of aborting — a serializability violation, silent.

state.oldest_version is set at init (server.ex:86) and never advanced by the sweep nor consulted during resolution.

Fix shape (FDB parity): sweep advances oldest_version; resolve aborts any transaction whose read_version < oldest_version (transaction_too_old), same as storage's version_too_old contract. A transaction older than the MVCC window must be impossible to commit, not silently unchecked.

Repro sketch: commit T1 writing key K at version V; wait > 6s (or shrink version_retention_ms); submit T2 with read_version < V reading K (read conflict on K) — T2 commits despite the conflicting write, because the V entry was swept.

Related: this floor is one enforcement point of the MVCC-window/read-version-lease contract being designed under bedrock-q67 (see q67.20 discussion), but the fix is independent and needed regardless.
title: Resolver silently skips conflict detection for read versions older than pruned history
